The Danish annual report taxonomies, as tables

Source: R/taxonomy_data.R
cvrr_taxonomy_tables.Rd

Every statement line of every entry point of twelve taxonomies, with the dimension defaults that say what an untagged figure means, prepared so that a filing can be given its labels and its structure without a taxonomy package on disk.

Format

cvrr_line, 61,584 rows – every statement line of every taxonomy:

version

The taxonomy, as "20231001".

entry

The entry point, where a statement is presented differently by different ones. NA for the 562 that are not.

statement

"BalanceSheetAccountForm", "IncomeStatementByNature", and so on.

code

The line's position, as "501.00.020.100". Ordering and containment are both read from it.

depth

Its depth in the presentation tree.

namespace

The concept's namespace URI – half of the key a filing is joined on, because a filer binds prefixes freely and e means fsa in one filing and sob in another.

elementid

The concept's name, without a prefix.

label

Its Danish label, as that version gives it.

balance

"debit", "credit" or NA: the direction a figure contributes, which is what find_signs() otherwise has to search for.

periodtype

"instant" or "duration".

is_total, is_leaf, abstract

As the presentation declares them.

cvrr_entry, 2,837 rows – which statements an entry point offers:

version, entry

The taxonomy and its entry point schema.

statement

One row per statement offered.

cvrr_default, 301 rows – the member that applies when a dimension is absent:

version

The taxonomy.

dimension

The dimension, as "cmn:ConsolidatedSoloDimension".

default_member

What an untagged figure means, as "cmn:SoloMember".

The last is small and easy to overlook, and it decides what a figure is. The consolidated/solo dimension defaults to solo, so a filing that tags nothing is stating the parent company's column – which is why add_taxonomy() can give every figure a basis. Leaving it out of these tables gave every figure a basis of NA, and every check that reads the parent column filtered on a value that was never there: the balance sheet went from 4,267 validated to nought, silently, because nothing errored.

Source

The taxonomy packages published by Erhvervsstyrelsen: thirteen versions, 20101108 to 20251001. The oldest contributes a dimension default and no statement lines at all, so cvrr_line and cvrr_entry hold twelve versions and cvrr_default thirteen.

The URI in a filing's schemaRef is an identifier and not an address – that host answers 404 for every version, the current ones included – so the packages come from Erhvervsstyrelsen's Taksonomier pages.

These tables are a convenience, not the only route. A version published after this release is read from the package itself with read_taxonomy() and passed to add_taxonomy(), and a filing declaring one the tables do not hold keeps its facts either way – see add_taxonomy().

Why two tables and not one, and why not three

A taxonomy offers around a dozen entry points – balance sheet in account form or report form, income statement by nature or by function, with or without the management's review – and they share their statements. Each line therefore appears about four times in a flat table. Of 579 version-and-statement pairs, 539 are offered by several entry points and presented identically by every one of them, 23 by a single entry point, and only 17 genuinely differ. Those 17 are prose and sector-specific disclosures – ManagementsReview, GeneralAndSubmissionData, the statements for investment funds and insurers – and none of the statements this package reconciles is among them. They keep an entry of their own; the rest have NA. 239,595 rows become 61,584.

A third table, one row per element carrying its label, balance and period type, was tried and taken out again. It looked like an obvious saving – those attributes barely move between versions – but a filing names its taxonomy in its schemaRef and is entitled to that version's answer, and they do move: balance for 11 elements, periodtype for 19, label for 275. Under xz the columns compress away regardless: with them on the line the data is 0.18 MB, and without them it was also 0.18 MB. The split cost correctness and saved nothing.

What genuinely varies is where a line sits. The code moves between versions for 10.9% of element-and-statement pairs, and every step check_cascade() derives comes from codes, so nothing is merged across versions.

See also

add_taxonomy(), which joins a filing to these, and read_taxonomy() for a package these do not yet hold.
